extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded mechanism adjudication from primary MD/CD/SPR/biological-activity sections, figure captions, and recovered OA supplementary PDF; claims are scoped to membrane-interaction/phenotype evidence and do not assert a single molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MD simulations support peptide-dependent differences in early interaction/positioning with neutral DLPC and anionic POPE:POPG membrane models, providing mechanistic context for membrane interaction rather than direct killing proof.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational membrane positioning is supportive context and is not treated as a standalone direct antimicrobial mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD and SPR evidence supports differential structuring and binding of kiadin peptides with model liposomes, including neutral-membrane binding, aggregation or LUV disruption patterns for selected peptides.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: diPGLa-H and kiadin-1 through kiadin-6 interacting with DOPC/DPPG or DOPC LUVs
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model-liposome binding/structuring is mechanism context; it does not prove a single molecular target or exact pore model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Table 2 supports peptide-specific antibacterial potency differences against E. coli and S. aureus, discussed as depending on glycine position and sequence context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: diPGLa-H and kiadin-1 through kiadin-6 against E. coli ATCC 25922 and S. aureus ATCC 25923
mechanism_claims.limitations: MIC/MBC phenotypes support potency differences but do not alone establish the molecular lesion.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: HC50/IC50 values and Figure 9 support peptide-specific host-cell toxicity patterns, which the authors relate cautiously to neutral liposome binding and MD insertion context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: human erythrocytes and MEC-1 cells exposed to diPGLa-H/kiadin peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Toxicity correlations are cautious; no direct molecular target in host cells is assigned.
